Thrice elected to the high pusition of•Grand l\faster, by his enlightened judgment
and wise and prudent administration, he promoted the best interests of the Craftexemplifying in his life and conduct the virtues and charities inculcated by our Order.

"Office of the Grand Master of ,lfasons,
" Stockton, May 2d, ,A. L. 5866.

"To the Masters,.Wardens, and Brethren of the several Lodges in this jurisdiction,
and especially to the Master, Wardens, and Brethren of - - Lodge, No. - :
"BRETHREN :-The duty confided to me, requiring that. I shall exercise a general
and careful supervision over the Craft, and see that the Cl>nstitution and Regnlat.ioni;
of the Grand Lodge are strictly maintained, supported, and obeyed, urges me to call
your attention to certain edicts promulgated at various Annual Communications,
whereby it is intended to render more perfect and uniform the system of work and
lectures. It bas always been a strong desire and the earnest purpose of the Grand
Lodge to secure, as far .as practica\Jle, uniformity of language and ceremony in all
the esoteric proceedings of our Fraternity. Next to harmonious sentiment, harmonious. and uniform action in the working of the Lodges is essential. For the accomplishment of this dssirable end, after mature deliberation and the careful consideration of a committee of experienced brethren appointed for the purpose, the following Regulation, with others, was adopted at the Annual Communication in May,
1863, viz. :"'Resolved, That, after due and timely notice has been given the Lodges under
this jurisdiction of the work and appointment of the Grand Lecturer and Deputy
Grand Lecturers, and said Lodges have had full opportunity to obtain instruction in
said system of work and lectul'es, an.v Lodg~ neglecting or refusing to learn and nse
such work, so approved and adopted by this Grand Lodge, shall, on proper representation of the facts to the Grand Master, be liable to the arrest of its charter, (if in
his discretion he shall think proper,) until they shall conform in all things to the regulations of the Grand Lodge in the premises.'
"And afterward, 11t the Communication held in October, 186!l, the following other
Regulation was adopted, viz.:,
"' Resol'Ced, That the action of the Grand Master, and· of the committee appointed
by him. for the examination and revision of the work and lectures, in accordance
with th't resolutions adopted at the last Annual Communication of this Grand Lodge,
together with the appointment by him of a Grand Lecturer and Deputies, be approved; and that the work in the three degrees, in all its parts, as exemplified by
the Grand Lecturer at this Communication, be approved, adopted, and made obligatory upon all subordinate Lodges within this jurisdiction.'
"Under these regulations the work and lectures, as revised and corrected, have
been regularly exemplified in Grand Lodge, and Ueputy Grand Lecturers have been
qualified and appointed in many parts of the jurisdiction to disseminate the work
and correct such errors as they might discover. I am pleased to say that their labors
have been attended with gratifying success. Further appointments will be made
from time to time, whenever zealous and capable brethren qualify themselves for the
important duty, and their ability to instruct is approved, by the Grand Lecturer.

CONSTITUTION OF THE GRAND LODGE,

RETURNS

Adopted October, A. L. 6866.

OF THE

Insert in the fifth line of Sec. 4, Art. III, Part 3, after the word" vote," the words
" by ballot" ; so that that section will read as follows :SECTION 4. No dispensation shall be issued to a Lodge to ballot for and confer the
degrees upon a candidate, without reference to a committee as provided in the preceding section, nor to receive and act upon the petition of a rejected applicant within
less than twelve months after the date of such rejection, unless the application therefor be made by the Lodge, by an unanimous vote by ballot; and of the special meet·
ing to be holden' under such dispensation, and the purpose thereof, the members of
the Lodge shall have due notice.

AMENDMENT TO THE GENERAL REGULATIONS
Adopted October, A. L. 15866.
The sixteenth of the General Regulations of the Grand Lodge was so amended as
to read as follows.:REouLATION 16. Non-affiliated Masons, who are suspended by operation of Sec. 1,
.Art. II, Part V, of the Constitution, if they desire to restore themsejves by afjiliatic:m,
shall pay a sum equivalent to six months dues, in addition to the affiliation fee re·
quired by the by-laws of the J,odge to which they may apply; or, if they desire to
restore themselves by contribution, they shall pay a sum equivalent to the amount of
the regular dues of the Lodge within whose jurisdiction they reside, during the whole
period of such residence ; unless sickness or inability to pay be shown as the reason
for such non-affiliation or non·payment.

ADDITIONAL GENERAL REGULATION,
Adopted October, A. L. 6866.
REGULATION 20. Whenever it is the intention of a person, who has been expelled
from the rights and privileges of Masonry, to petition the Grand Lodge for restora·
tion, it shall be his duty to notify the Lodge which expelled him of such intention,
at least sixty days before the meeting of the Grand Lodge, accompanying said notice
with a copy of his intended petition ; and before said petition shall be considered by
the Grand Lodge, proof shall be made of the giving of 11aid notice.
